## strategies
[ace-0001] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: Before implementing a new function, read the existing module and its helpers (e.g. money utilities like to_money/round_money/ZERO) and reuse them so rounding and type conventions stay consistent with the rest of the codebase.
[ace-0002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: For weighted-average or division-based functions, guard against a zero denominator (e.g. empty lines / total quantity 0) and return the domain's zero constant rather than raising.
## common_mistakes
[ace-0003] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: When summing Decimal values, pass an explicit start value (e.g. sum(..., ZERO)) instead of relying on the default int 0, to avoid type mixing and preserve money semantics.

item.content: When validating an integer parameter, explicitly reject bool (isinstance(x, bool)) before the int check, since Python treats True/False as ints and would otherwise pass a positive-integer guard.

Match the error codes and message style of sibling functions in the same module (e.g. reuse 'invalid_state' with the same f-string format) so new validation is consistent with existing callers and tests.
Don't assume a helper like to_money accepts arbitrary input; verify its behavior for strings/floats and rely on it to raise the domain error (e.g. invalid_amount) rather than duplicating type checks.
